title: How Hailstones Grow Bigger Than a Grapefruit
description: The biggest hailstone measured in the United States fell in South Dakota in 2010 and was about 20 centimetres wide. Here's how a storm builds one.
comment: What's the biggest hail you've ever seen?

scenes.narration: In 2010, a hailstone 20 centimetres wide fell in South Dakota.
Every hailstone starts as a tiny frozen droplet high inside a thunderstorm.
Strong winds inside the storm carry it up through freezing water, again and again.
Each trip adds another layer of ice, like the rings of an onion.
When it's too heavy for the wind to hold up, it falls.
The biggest ones need updrafts of more than 150 kilometres an hour to grow that large.
